title: Permission Simulation Playbook and Golden-States Regression Orchestrator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Ship a robust permission simulation playbook and an automated golden-state regression orchestrator for RBAC v2 that verifies permission enforcement across runtime, console, and private deployments. The orchestrator will exercise SSO/SAML assertions, admin UI controls, and audit logging to detect regressions early in CI and nightly runs. Scope includes: (1) a matrix-driven simulator that generates authorized/unauthorized traffic for user, service, and admin principals; (2) a canonical golden-fixtures set representing expected authorization outcomes and audit log entries; (3) a comparer that asserts policy decisions and audit trail integrity; (4) CI integration and a nightly regression job with alerting and a human review workflow for golden updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can generate 1,000 unique request permutations across roles, resources, and actions and assert decision outcomes against golden fixtures
Audit log comparator validates presence, actor, resource, decision, and reason fields for 95% of executed permutations
SSO/SAML assertion test harness validates mapping of incoming SAML attributes to RBAC role claims for at least two IdP providers (Okta, Azure AD) in CI
Admin control end-to-end test covers enabling/disabling a role and verifies downstream enforcement within 60s
Nightly regression job runs successfully, posts a summary to #sec-ci and opens a triage ticket automatically on >0 unexpected diffs
tasks: Design permission matrix and canonical golden fixtures (roles x resources x actions)
Implement simulator binary (go) that can replay permutations as bearer tokens and as SAML assertions
Build golden-comparer library that normalizes runtime responses and audit log records for deterministic comparison
Integrate simulator and comparer into CI (GitHub Actions) and add nightly Datadog monitor for diffs
Create manual update playbook for golden fixture changes with required approvals and audit trail
deliverables: golden-fixtures v1 JSON set under infra/testdata/goldens/rbac-v2/v1
comparer library and assertion rules under internal/authz/testutils
Confluence playbook: Permission Simulation & Golden Update Runbook
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use matrix-driven tests rather than exhaustive combinatorics to keep CI runtime reasonable (tradeoff: lower coverage vs faster feedback)
Record audit-log expectations as normalized fields (actor, resource, verb, decision, reason) to minimize brittle diffs when non-deterministic fields (timestamps, request-ids) change
Run full permutation set only nightly; PRs run a deterministic sampled subset chosen by risk/area impacted

SSO/SAML assertions will be tested using signed SAML responses generated by a local IdP emulator for CI; we accepted some fidelity loss vs running against SaaS IdPs to avoid flakiness and secrets in CI
implementation_notes: Simulator supports two modes: bearer-token (JWT) and saml-assertion (base64 XML). Use same permission matrix to generate inputs for both
Golden fixtures are keyed by stable resource identifiers (resource_type:resource_id) to reduce churn from ephemeral resource names
Comparer will apply stable canonicalization: remove timestamp/uuid fields, sort array fields, and map equivalent decision texts to standardized tokens
Audit logging integration requires a small runtime hook (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876) to emit canonicalized events to /debug/golden-logs during test runs
Add feature flag to enable golden-mode in dedicated/private deployments so nightly regressions can run against staging fleets without impacting production telemetry
ci_integration: Primary GH Actions job: rbac-golden-sample - runs sampled permutations on PRs (timeout 25m)
Nightly GH Actions job: rbac-golden-nightly - runs full golden suite and uploads results to S3
On diff: create a GitHub issue template pre-filled with failing permutations, attach normalized diffs, and notify #sec-ci and #platform-oncall
Datadog Synthetic: monitor parity_count metric; alert when unexpected_diffs > 0 for two consecutive runs

notes_for_triage: When a diff is detected: (1) triage must attach normalized diff JSON, (2) owner must run simulator locally against the same commit and attach logs, (3) if golden change is legitimate, update golden fixtures and require two approvals (security + product) before merge
Keep golden fixtures small and human-readable; store expanded test vectors in a separate archive to avoid CI bloat
Plan a maintenance cadence: rotate golden fixtures quarterly and after major policy changes
